import.title: Import transactions
import.intro_caption: Pick the platform, then upload its statement. Rows are parsed and validated; nothing is written until you commit. Duplicates against the ledger are flagged, not removed — wipe first for a clean re-import of an overlapping export.
import.toast_cleared: All imports cleared — the ledger is empty.
import.metric_value_help: What the holdings are worth at the latest close; a name with no price is carried at cost. The same figure as the Portfolio overview.
import.metric_injected_help: What you put in from your own pocket, less what you took out — money collected from a sale counts as taken out.
import.metric_dividends_help: Every dividend the ledger has booked, gross, each at its own date's rate.
import.clear_all_confirm: Delete **all {n} transactions** from your ledger? Positions, realized gains and tax reports all derive from it, so the portfolio resets to empty — as if nothing was ever imported. This cannot be undone.
import.drop_title: Drag and drop the statement here
import.drop_replace: Drop another file or browse to replace it
import.paste_expander: No upload? Paste the statement instead
import.paste_caption: Some browsers and work devices block the file picker outright, and a browser that drops this app's cookies fails the upload with a 403 you never see. Dragging the file onto the box above usually still works — and if it doesn't, paste the export here instead, header line included: it is parsed, previewed and committed exactly like an upload. A PDF or XLSX can't be pasted as text: upload it as a file, or export the statement as CSV.
import.paste_placeholder: Paste the whole export, starting with its header line
import.paste_blocked: Your browser is not sending this app's cookie, so an upload would be rejected before it reaches the page. Paste the statement here instead.
import.paste_wrong_type: That is a {kind} file, and {platform} statements are read as {types} here. Export it in one of those formats, or paste the text version.
import.rows_no_longer: {n} of those rows are no longer in the ledger (deleted or wiped since).
import.last_import_help: **Clear last import** deletes exactly these rows from the ledger — no re-upload needed. **Dismiss** only forgets this note; the ledger stays.
import.no_rows_parsed: No rows parsed — is this a {platform} statement? {hint}
import.wrong_type: That is a {kind} file, and statements are read as {types} here. Export it in one of those formats, or paste the text version.
import.nothing_read: Nothing in this file reads as a transaction — not to the AI, nor to any parser. Is this a {platform} statement? {hint}
import.read_as: Read as {label}, not {picked}: its parser recognised the file.
import.read_by_model: Read by the AI: no parser here knows this layout. Check the rows before you commit them.
import.read_positions: This is a holdings report, not a list of trades — nothing in it is dated, so there is nothing to import. Export the transactions statement instead.
import.read_model_off: The AI could not be reached, so only the built-in parsers read this file.
import.rejected_help: Fix these rows in the statement and upload it again — or paste its text under “No upload? Paste the statement instead” and fix them there.
import.skipped_rows: Skipped rows ({n}) — by design, nothing lost
import.skipped_caption_revolut: Cash movements, rewards and dividend-tax corrections don't affect positions. Splits are auto-resolved when the ratio is derivable; underivable ones stay here — add those manually.
import.skipped_caption_generic: Each row lists why it couldn't become a transaction — fix the CSV and re-upload, or add those rows manually.
import.broker_help: This format names no broker, so pick the one the file came from — or type its name if it isn't listed. It is stamped on every row; the Fees and Custody views group your book by it.
import.file_too_large: That file is {size} MB, and statements are capped at {cap} MB. Export a narrower date range, or split it in two — nothing has been uploaded.
import.unreadable: This device could not open that file, so nothing was uploaded. If it lives in Drive or came from a chat app, save it to the phone's Downloads first and pick it from there — or paste its contents below.
import.file_changed: The file changed since the preview. Check it again before confirming.
import.commit_failed: The portfolio may have moved since the preview — check it again, then retry.
import.commit_help: Committed rows persist in the ledger across reloads — no need to re-upload. Open **Portfolio** for positions & tax, or **Overview** to see your buys/sells on the price chart.
import.sample_caption: No {platform} statement to hand? Try the app with an example one — it is parsed, previewed and committed exactly like yours, and undone with **Clear last import**.
import.demo_rows_caption: {n} of these are demo transactions. Importing a statement removes them.
import.scan_splits_help: Statements print trades, not the splits between them. A position bought before a split and never sold keeps its old share count and cost basis until the split is added.
import.scan_splits_clean: No missing splits — every holding's share count is on today's scale.
import.splits_found: {n} split(s) your ledger is missing. Until they are added, these holdings show a pre-split share count and an inflated average buy price:
import.split_evidence: bought at {price} on {date}, when the split-adjusted close was {close}
import.apply_splits: Add {n} split row(s) to the ledger
import.apply_splits_help: Each row multiplies the shares held on its date; the money paid is unchanged, so the average buy price falls by the same ratio. Check the resulting share count against your broker — a statement that skipped the split may also have skipped later sales.
import.moves_found: {n} holding(s) look like they only changed broker, not owner. Your statement records the departure as a sale, so the book reports a gain nobody made and restarts the holding period:
import.move_basis: arrived carrying a cost of {basis}, not the {sold} it was booked as sold at
import.apply_moves_help: The sale rows become transfers: no gain is realized, the original purchase dates and cost stay, and both brokers' labels for the security are unified. Nothing else about the rows changes.
import.lede: Pick a platform, upload the statement, check every row and confirm. **Nothing is written to your portfolio until you confirm.**
import.wipe_short_note: a clean re-import; asks for your email
import.wipe_warning: All {n} transactions will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
import.wipe_warning_one: The {n} transaction will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
import.wipe_safer: To remove only the last import, use “Clear the last import”: it undoes exactly those rows.
import.wipe_type_commit: Type **{email}** to be able to confirm the import
import.tier_warned_note: imported; also in the full list
import.tier_importable_note: what will be written to your portfolio, warned rows included
import.tier_skipped_note: left out by design; nothing is lost
import.skip_cash_note: money in or out of the account; no position changes
import.skip_reward_note: a cash credit; no position changes
import.skip_interest_note: a cash credit; no position changes
import.skip_fx_note: cash from one currency to another; no position changes
import.skip_fee_note: add them by hand if you want them in the cost
import.skip_unknown_note: a type this importer does not read; not imported
import.skip_not_stock_note: options, futures, FX and the like are not imported
import.skip_staking_note: the same coins, neither bought nor sold; nothing to import
import.skip_accrued_note: not paid yet; they import from the statement that covers the pay date
import.skip_split_note: the ratio could not be worked out; add them by hand
import.skip_div_tax_note: they arrive in +/- pairs that cancel out; check them by hand
import.skip_coin_reward_note: no price for that day could be found; it is an acquisition at market value (taxable income in Spain), so add each as a buy at that day's price
import.skip_coin_swap_note: fiscally a sale plus a purchase; add both legs by hand at that day's prices
import.skip_coin_transfer_note: coins moved without a price; adjust by hand if one was a disposal
import.skip_crypto_cash_note: money in or out of the exchange; only the coins are tracked
import.skip_crypto_internal_note: staking, savings or wallet transfers of the same coins; nothing bought or sold
import.skip_crypto_not_coin_note: shares or metals in a crypto app's export; import those from their own statement
import.skip_crypto_unpriced_note: no market close to value it at; add it by hand with that day's price
import.skip_crypto_fee_note: paid in a coin with no price that day; add it as the fee on its row if you want it in the cost
import.skip_crypto_unsupported_note: a code with no market price here; add it by hand if it matters
import.skip_crypto_unreadable: Rows that could not be read
import.skip_crypto_unreadable_note: a date, type, amount or side missing or unclear; add these by hand
import.skip_withholding_note: set each as the fee on its dividend row, for the double-tax credit
import.skip_degiro_portfolio_note: today's holdings, with no trades and no purchase price. In DEGIRO: Activity → Transactions → Export → CSV, and upload that file
import.skip_degiro_account_note: the cash statement, with no trades. In DEGIRO: Activity → Transactions → Export → CSV, and upload that file
import.skip_other_note: each says why it could not become a transaction; fix the export and upload it again, or add them by hand
import.rejected_fix: Fix these rows in the statement and upload it again — or paste its text under “No upload? Paste the statement instead” and fix them there.
import.unlisted_note: Yahoo lists none of {tickers} under these codes. They import, but hold at cost with no price until you pick the market each one trades on.
import.unlisted_note_one: Yahoo does not list {tickers} under this code. It imports, but holds at cost with no price until you pick the market it trades on.
import.gain_buy: against today's price, the fee counted in the cost
import.gain_sell: realized, against the FIFO cost of the shares sold
import.confirm_rows: **{n} rows** will be written to your portfolio.
import.confirm_rows_one: **{n} row** will be written to your portfolio.
import.confirm_left_both: The rejected ({rejected}) and the skipped ({skipped}) are not.
import.commit_needs_email: Type your email under “Empty the portfolio” to confirm.
import.nothing_written: Nothing was imported. Your portfolio is as it was.
import.moves_note: They leave the statement as sales: the portfolio counts a gain that does not exist.
import.splits_note: A statement never prints splits. A holding bought before one keeps its old share count and price until you add it.
import.splits_throttled: No data: Yahoo is rate-limiting. That does not mean nothing is missing.
import.rows_gone: {n} rows are no longer in your portfolio
import.rows_gone_one: {n} row is no longer in your portfolio
import.last_help_short: Clearing undoes exactly that import. Dismissing hides this note and keeps the rows.
import.sample_short: No statement to hand? Try the flow with an example one: it is read, reviewed and confirmed exactly like yours, and “Clear the last import” undoes it.
import.guest: Sign in to import your statements.
import.venue_none: No {currency} market found for this code.
import.work_venues: Finding its markets and their prices
import.venue_against: Your latest fill: {price} on {day}. Each market's close that day:
import.venue_nothing: Nothing in {currency} for “{query}”. Try the company's name.
import.venue_refused: {symbol} cannot be saved for this code: it did not close near your fills, or the code is already priced. Search again.
import.venue_retry: Yahoo did not answer. Try again in a minute.
import.venue_throttled: Yahoo is refusing requests right now, so “no price” may just mean it did not answer.
